renderer.identification: Renderer metadata plus FunctionCall source locations for the loopback greenhouse app and benchmark; source URLs omitted.

sample_window.alignment: Reused saved CDP Timestamp/Date.now clock pair on the same host. The earlier baseline clock pair differs by 2.595 ms. Native trace has no direct wall-clock sync; alignment assumes no intervening clock adjustment and is approximate. Benchmark completion callback independently lies at the expected window end.
sample_window.task_selection: Only fully contained complete RunTask events; boundary-crossing tasks excluded without prorating thread CPU.

sample_boundary_report_task.interpretation: End-of-sample task contains report generation; excluded from sampled gameplay task aggregates.

interpretation: Six gameplay renderer-main tasks exceed 20 ms; none exceeds 50 ms. Their wall times are much larger than their measured thread CPU times.
Wall minus thread CPU establishes elapsed time not executing on this thread; this capture cannot distinguish descheduling, blocking, or native driver waits.
One nested GPU-client Flush lasts about 9.6 ms with about 0.08 ms thread CPU; this localizes part of one smaller stall but does not establish a GPU bottleneck.
The 293 ms hitch was not reproduced, so its cause remains unproven.
limitations: RunTask wall and tdur values are inclusive; nested events are illustrative and must not be added to task totals.
A small number of tasks lack tdur; these are counted separately, never interpreted as zero CPU.
No OS scheduler trace is available; System Trace is currently unavailable on this host.
Only the identified greenhouse renderer process is summarized; the shared GPU process is not attributed to this page.
next_diagnostic: Repeat the available short Chromium native trace capture when the large hitch occurs; compare RunTask wall/tdur and nested GPU-client flush/wait spans. Distinguishing blocking from descheduling still requires scheduler/native wait evidence not present here.
